title: Alibaba Debuts What It Calls China's Most Powerful AI Chip and a 20-Gigawatt Global Cloud Buildout
subhead: At its Apsara conference, Alibaba unveiled a flagship AI chip and teased a 10-trillion-parameter model while mapping cloud capacity past 20 GW by 2032 — the clearest signal yet that China's cloud giants are moving to close the domestic compute gap as Trump hosts Xi in Washington this week.

sections.heading: Alibaba Unveils 'China's Most Powerful' AI Chip and Teases a 10-Trillion-Parameter Model
sections.body:
At the opening of its annual Apsara Conference in Hangzhou on Tuesday, Alibaba Group unveiled what it called China's most powerful AI chip and outlined plans to train an AI model with up to 10 trillion parameters, according to the South China Morning Post and Nikkei Asia. Group chairman Joe Tsai framed the move around building 'full-stack AI,' while CEO Eddie Wu Yongming identified 'AI models, AI chips and the AI cloud' as the three cornerstones of the machine-intelligence era.

The company targets scaling Alibaba Cloud's global data-center capacity to more than 20 gigawatts by 2032, a major step up in ambition that signals Alibaba intends to compete not just on models but on the physical compute infrastructure underneath them.
sections.whyItMatters: This is the most direct bid yet by a Chinese cloud giant to supply its own training-grade silicon rather than depend on foreign GPUs, and it pairs hardware with an audacious model scale target. It reframes China's domestic-compute push from chip announcements into a full-stack, hyperscale buildout timed right before the Washington summit.

sections.heading: Semiconductors: Bernstein Says Huawei's Kirin 9050 Pro Narrowed the Gap With Apple to About Three Years
sections.body: Equity research firm Bernstein estimated in a note covered by the South China Morning Post that Huawei's new Kirin 9050 Pro smartphone processor — unveiled earlier this month and produced using technology equivalent to roughly a 7-nanometre node — has cut Huawei's performance deficit versus Apple's chips to about three years, down from roughly four years in the previous generation. The chip beat Apple's 2023-era 3nm A17 Pro in Geekbench 6 multicore tests, though it remained around 30 percent behind Apple's newest 2nm A20 Pro, with single-core performance closer to TSMC-made designs.
sections.whyItMatters: The narrowing is incremental rather than revolutionary — Huawei is still roughly a generation-plus behind on advanced nodes — but the trajectory matters because it quantifies how quickly Chinese fabs and designers are closing the performance gap despite export controls. The 30 percent deficit also gives a concrete measure of how far the domestic ecosystem still has to go.

sections.heading: Hygon Expands From Data Centers Into Robotics and Physical AI
sections.body: Chinese chipmaker Hygon Information Technology on Tuesday launched its Hygon 1000 series — a suite of embedded central processing units for robotics and industrial edge devices — marking a push beyond cloud computing into physical AI, per the South China Morning Post. Built on Hygon's x86-compatible C86 architecture, the four-core, eight-thread CPUs support both DDR4 and DDR5 memory and are aimed at industrial automation, robots and factory controllers where compute and graphics processing are handled locally.
sections.whyItMatters: China's domestic chip road map is broadening beyond data centers and smartphones into the physical world — robotics, factory floors and edge AI. That widens the surface where domestic architectures can substitute for foreign chips, extending the push for self-reliance into what Beijing has framed as 'physical intelligence.'

sections.heading: Subsea Cables: NEC Joins Meta's 'Petal' in a Bid for the World's First Petabit-Class US-France Line
sections.body: Japanese group NEC is handling design and construction for Meta Platforms' Petal subsea cable project connecting the United States and France, an effort the companies are positioning toward the world's first petabit-class underwater connection as AI traffic booms, according to Nikkei Asia. The project rides a wave of cable investment driven by data-center expansion and rising concerns over the resilience of undersea infrastructure.
sections.whyItMatters: Subsea cables are the physical backbone of AI compute, and a petabit-class transatlantic link is a statement of intent about capacity for cross-border model training and data movement. NEC's role also highlights Japan's growing position in high-end cable engineering at a moment when the vulnerability of undersea links — a running theme in Mideast coverage — is moving up security agendas.

sections.heading: Space: Sharp Builds a Multi-Network Antenna to Challenge Starlink's Lock-In
sections.body: Sharp plans to develop an antenna that can connect to multiple different satellite communications networks, letting users switch between services rather than depend on specific providers such as SpaceX's Starlink, according to Nikkei Asia on Wednesday. Sharp, which already supplies satellite receivers offering both low-Earth and geostationary links and has taken orders for AI servers backed by Foxconn's supply chain, is positioning itself for demand driven by the push for alternative connectivity.
sections.whyItMatters: A universal, multi-network antenna is a direct answer to the proprietary lock-in that defines the satellite-broadband market today, where Starlink dominates. It reflects broader pressure — from governments and enterprises — for choice and resilience in satellite connectivity as constellations multiply.

sections.heading: Alternative Compute: Amazon Teams With TBC to Train AI on Living Neurons
sections.body: Amazon is working with San Francisco startup The Biological Computing Co. (TBC), which uses roughly 100,000 living neurons — some dissected from rat brains, others grown from human skin cells — fused to a grid of 4,096 electrodes, to make AI models faster and cheaper, per Nikkei Asia. TBC's new model is reported to boost video-generation speed fivefold, a claim the company ties to its biocomputing approach.
sections.whyItMatters: The deal is a bet on an exotic, early-stage alternative to silicon as the ceiling on conventional GPU training costs and power use comes into view. It is early and unproven, but the involvement of a hyperscaler signals that major players are willing to explore radical compute paths to cut the cost of large models.

sections.heading: Diplomatic Track: Trump Hosts Xi This Week With the Trade Truce Expiring and AI High on the Agenda
sections.body: U.S. President Donald Trump is set to host Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping for a state visit in Washington this week with a packed agenda covering trade and AI and an expiry date on the rival powers' trade truce fast approaching, according to Nikkei Asia. Nikkei separately reports Xi skipped delivering a UN address in New York, a decision framed as an assertion of status as an equal of the United States rather than a guest paying deference on the global stage.
sections.whyItMatters: The summit gives a hard deadline to the running questions on export controls and AI governance. With Alibaba, Huawei and Hygon all making fresh domestic-compute moves days before the meeting, the timing is a reminder that China is racing to shore up its own stack while the two leaders sit down to negotiate the terms of coexistence.

bottomLine: Wednesday's biggest move is Alibaba treating China's domestic AI stack as a full hyperscale buildout — a flagship chip, a 10-trillion-parameter target and 20 GW of global cloud capacity by 2032 — rather than a series of isolated chips. It lands alongside incremental but real progress in the semiconductor race (Huawei's Kirin narrowing the gap with Apple to about three years, per Bernstein), a widening of domestic chipmaking into robotics, and fresh investment in the physical layers of connectivity (Meta and NEC's petabit-class subsea cable, Sharp's multi-network satellite antenna). The backdrop is the Washington summit, where Trump and Xi sit down this week with the trade truce expiring; Beijing appears to be using every lever — compute, hardware, connectivity — to arrive at the negotiating table with a more self-sufficient stack in hand.
sources: Nikkei Asia (Alibaba AI chip/20GW, NEC Petal subsea cable, Sharp satellite antenna, Amazon-TBC biocomputing, Trump-Xi summit), South China Morning Post (Alibaba Apsara chip and 10T model, Hygon robotics CPUs, Huawei Kirin 9050 Pro Bernstein)
